parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Experiment 1
Use a measuring cylinder to pour 10cm of dilute hydrochloric acid into a boiling tube. Put the
boiling tube into a rack for support.
Measure the temperature of the hydrochloric acid and record it in the table below.
Add 1g of zinc to the boiling tube and stir the mixture with the thermometer.
Measure and record the maximum temperature reached by the mixture. Pour the mixture away
and rinse the boiling tube.
Experiment 2
Repeat Experiment 1 using 1g of iron instead of zinc.
Record your results in the table.
Experiment 3
Repeat Experiment 1 using 1g of magnesium instead of zinc.
Record your results in the table. Complete the final column in the table.

Experiment 4
Use a measuring cylinder to pour 10cm of copper(II) sulfate solution into a boiling tube.
Measure the temperature of the solution and record it in the table on page 3.
Add 1g of magnesium to the boiling tube and stir the mixture with the thermometer.
Test the gas given off with a splint and record your result in the space below. Measure the
maximum temperature reached by the mixture and record it in the table. Pour the mixture away
and rinse the boiling tube.

text: You are going to investigate what happens when dilute hydrochloric acid and copper(II) sulfate
solution react with different metals.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to carry out five experiments.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add several drops of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the first portion of the solution and
shake the test-tube.
Now add excess aqueous sodium hydroxide to the test-tube.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Using the second portion of the solution, repeat the test in (a)(i) using aqueous ammonia
instead of aqueous sodium hydroxide.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid to the third portion of the solution followed by about
1cm of aqueous silver nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Pour the fourth portion of the solution into a boiling tube.
Add about 1cm of aqueous sodium hydroxide and a small piece of aluminium foil.
Warm the mixture carefully and test the gas given off.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify solid G.

tests on the residue

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Use a spatula to transfer some of the residue into a test-tube.
To the residue, add about 2cm of dilute hydrochloric acid. Test any gases given off.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Carry out a flame test on the residue.
Record your observations.

text: You are provided with a mixture of two solids, G and H.
Solid G is water soluble and solid H is insoluble in water.
Carry out the following tests on the mixture, recording all of your observations at each stage.
Add about 15cm of distilled water to the mixture in a boiling tube.
Shake the boiling tube for one minute. Filter the contents of the tube, keeping the filtrate and the
residue. Divide the filtrate into four equal portions in four test-tubes and carry out the following
tests.
tests on filtrate
Nickel sulfate-6-water, NiSO .6H O, is a blue crystalline salt.
Plan an experiment to obtain a sample of pure water from this salt. Your answer should include
a diagram of the apparatus, any expected observations and a test to show the presence of pure
water.
You are provided with common laboratory apparatus.
[Total: 6]
